messages:
maria-sre: alerting — seeing a rapid connection burst to embeddings.v1 from a small set of IPv6 ranges, SYN/half-open pattern. spike started ~1912345600, RTT low. tagging as potential volumetric/probing abuse. /cc @sam-security @devon-eng

sam-security: thanks. any sign of successful requests or elevated CPU on inference hosts? we should consider temporary WAF rule + per-ip rate limit. also want audit log entry for any ipset changes. :eyes:

devon-eng: hosts show large number of TCP SYNs, many not completing TLS handshake. CPU and GPU utilization fine — most requests never hit application layer. connection table growth seen on the edge proxies. logs: `tcp_flags=SYN, ack=0` and lots of different flow-ids but same ASNs. extracting pcap samples now.

ops-bot: automated countermeasure candidate: add ipset blocklist for offending prefixes, enable strict SYN cookies on edge, throttle connection rate to 20 conn/s per /64. approved=false by default. to execute: `/usr/local/bin/edge-mitigate --add-ipset <set> --rate 20`

maria-sre: provisional plan — 1) apply temporary ipset /64 block for top offending prefixes (manual review first), 2) enable SYN-cookie mode on proxy, 3) push a lightweight WAF rule to drop non-handshakes. keep canary in one region (us-west2) first.

sam-security: please add an audit log entry to the security-audit stream before we modify ipset. we need change provenance (who/why) for compliance. also we should sign the config snapshot with KMS key if we alter rules long-term.

ashley-platops: note — our current ipset-flip script runs under `platops` RBAC role. if someone from SRE will run this, we need a temporary escalation token or create a service principal with just ipset write perms. prefer service principal to human escalation.

devon-eng: pcap shows source ASN 39712 and a wide /32 range on IPv6. creating a small ipset and testing in us-west2:

```
# sample ipset add
ipset create abuse_v6 hash:net family inet6
ipset add abuse_v6 2001:db8:1234::/64
iptables -I INPUT -m set --match-set abuse_v6 src -j DROP
```

ops-bot: test run completed in canary — SYN incomplete rate dropped 92% in that region, connection table stabilized. ready to roll to global if approved.

sam-security: approve global roll if we also: 1) emit audit event to security-audit (kinesis) with action metadata, 2) attach KMS-signed snapshot of ipset content to the incident record, 3) schedule 24h staged removal check.

maria-sre: approved. @ashley-platops please create service principal `edge-mitigator@redwood` with ipset-write and audit-publish perms only. we will not grant blanket platops RBAC.

ashley-platops: creating principal now. also flagging a minor RBAC gap: audit-publish permission currently only exists for platform-admin role. will add granular permission `audit:publish` for service principals. will open a PR for RBAC changes and tag @sam-security for review.

deploy-bot: roll started 1912345840 -> pushed ipset entries to all regions, enabled SYN-cookie on proxies. note: one edge node had a transient config apply error — retried and succeeded at 1912345889.

karen-support: drafting customer comms for affected customers on embeddings endpoint. short message: "We observed abusive connection attempts from a small set of IPv6 ranges affecting connection success rates transiently. We've applied targeted network-level mitigations; customers may see improved reliability. No data access or model inference integrity impacts." sharing draft for review.

luis-customer-eng: tweak suggestion: call out that this was network-level throttling and provide guidance if customers see elevated 5xxs to open a support ticket with timestamps. include link to status page incident id once created.

maria-sre: post-incident actions: 1) formal postmortem (owners: devon + sam), 2) add telemetry alert on half-open handshake rate > 100/s, 3) automate ipset snapshot + KMS HSM signing on each change, 4) RBAC PR for `audit:publish` scoped to service principals, 5) add a runbook entry for SYN-flood on embeddings path. will assign tasks after call.

sam-security: also file a vuln triage to check whether any exposed proxy config made this easier to exploit (CVE tracker entry if needed). we should verify proxy versions and CVE DB quick scan.

maria-sre: thanks everyone. closing immediate thread — monitoring for 2 hours then transition to postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
